newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian opposition seeks parliamentary election.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian opposition seeks parliamentary election.

text.p: Bulgarian opposition leaders, basking in a presidential election win, said on Thursday they would press for early parliamentary polls to oust the cabinet they accuse of dragging its feet on IMF-backed reforms.

Ivan Kostov, leader of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), told reporters Sunday's run-off vote of almost 60 percent for reformist lawyer Petar Stoyanov showed the Socialist government had lost the confidence of the electorate halfway through its four-year term.

"The political council of the United Democratic Forces took a decision to start work for triggering an early parliamentary election," Kostov told reporters after a meeting of the alliance of opposition parties in parliament.
The leadership of the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) meets on Monday to discuss calls for cabinet changes and policy reforms.
The BSP is made up mainly of ex-communists who renamed the party after their hardline leader Todor Zhivkov was toppled in 1989 and remain closer to Moscow than to Brussels.
They have a secure majority in parliament. But Prime Minister Zhan Videnov's handling of the severe economic crisis is under fire from inside and outside the party.
Main trade unions are discussing a general strike to protest against falling living standards.

"If the BSP proposes a new cabinet we should not give it our confidence because the problem is not in Zhan Videnov's cabinet but in the whole policy of the party," said Stefan Savov, head of the smaller, UDF-allied People's Union.

A visiting IMF -- International Monetary Fund -- mission has proposed pegging the collapsing lev to the dollar or the mark through a currency board to help the authorities win back control of the economy and restore confidence.
The mission is discussing terms for release of a $115 million credit vital to avert default on Bulgaria's $10 billion foreign debt.

The funds have twice been delayed because of the government's failure to meet reform targets which include curbing inflation, stabilising the exchange rate, speeding up privatisation and closing loss-making enterprises.
